root_cause: report_date() takes the business date from the machine's local time zone (time.localtime), but business dates are defined in America/New_York. The CI job runs with TZ=UTC, so an order at 2026-03-01 03:30 UTC (22:30 on Feb 28 in New York) is filed under the wrong day. The same bug would hit any production host that isn't set to New York time.
evidence: repo/src/reports.py: time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d', time.localtime(epoch_seconds)), with docstring 'Uses the machine's local time zone'
repo/tests/test_reports.py comment: '2026-03-01 03:30 UTC is 2026-02-28 22:30 in New York (business time zone)'
Local check: with the patch, the test passes with TZ=UTC and TZ=Asia/Tokyo
patch:
--- a/src/reports.py
+++ b/src/reports.py
@@ -1,4 +1,9 @@
-import time
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
+
+BUSINESS_TZ = ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
+
 def report_date(epoch_seconds):
-    """Business date for a timestamp. Uses the machine's local time zone."""
-    return time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d", time.localtime(epoch_seconds))
+    """Business date for a timestamp, in the business time zone (America/New_York),
+    independent of the machine's local time zone."""
+    return datetime.fromtimestamp(epoch_seconds, tz=timezone.utc).astimezone(BUSINESS_TZ).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
message_to_human: report_date() uses the host's local time zone, but the test (and the business definition it documents) expects New York business dates. With TZ=UTC in CI, late-night New York orders land on the next day. That is a real bug on any UTC server, not just a CI quirk. This MR makes the business time zone explicit: it converts the epoch to an aware UTC datetime and then to ZoneInfo('America/New_York'), so the result no longer depends on the machine's TZ. I verified it under TZ=UTC and TZ=Asia/Tokyo. I didn't change CI's TZ, because that would hide the bug. Please confirm America/New_York is the correct business zone. Note that zoneinfo needs system tzdata or the tzdata package on hosts without it.
